answer: One concrete anti-Sybil defense locks a progressive stake per identity: each new agent must deposit tokens that remain frozen until a long cooldown expires. An attacker flooding the network faces capital that scales linearly with the number of identities, quickly becoming prohibitive. Imagine a river of fake agents trying to crest a high ledge of required deposits while a sudden zephyr of market volatility drains their liquid reserves; the cost forces the attacker to abandon the attempt long before consensus is threatened.
